correctness.rationale: After translating the support to (0,a,b), restriction of characters to H is onto, with N/h characters in each fiber; translation contributes only a nonzero phase. The two unit phases (u,v) on a,b distinguish local characters. The equation c_0+c_1u+c_2v=0 forces u to the intersection of a real line and the unit circle; c_0c_1≠0 makes the line condition nonconstant, and c_2≠0 determines v uniquely. For two distinct rows (1,u,v), the kernel is one projective ray, admissible exactly when its three cofactors are nonzero. This amounts to the character ratio being nontrivial on each of a,b,a-b. The three annihilators have pairwise intersection {1} because any two differences generate H; inclusion-exclusion gives L and unordered pair counting gives hL/2. Good ratios cannot be involutions, so L is even. If the three proper annihilators cover, none can be trivial; products of nonidentity elements from two embed injectively in the nonidentity part of the third. The three resulting size inequalities force all three proper subgroups to have order two and the group to be Klein four. Conversely its three annihilators cover. The zero and specified one-zero levels exist by avoiding finitely many proper hyperplanes/subspaces. Finally, every non-Klein H has an element of order at least three, so h≥q; the cyclic support (0,g,2g) for an element of least such order q reaches the bound, and the Klein-four contribution is attained separately when available. This proves all cases analytically. The frozen rational-phase script is a finite check, not relied on for universal coverage.

value.rationale: For the first support size at which two different character-zero conditions can determine a projective coefficient ray, the exact number and absence criterion are useful refinements of an uncertainty bound. The three annihilator sizes make the dependence on mixed torsion explicit and count choices even when two supports have identical extremal zero levels. This is a natural fixed-support classification and exact coefficient count, not an assertion about larger supports or restricted amplitude alphabets.
